subject: maths
title: Year 6 Number Patterns
seo_title: Year 6 Number Patterns Worksheets: Free Maths with Answer Key (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Recognise and use rules that generate visually growing patterns and number patterns involving rational numbers
meta_desc: Free Year 6 maths worksheets on number patterns, aligned to the Australian Curriculum (AC9M6A01): continue patterns with decimals and fractions, find the rule, growing matchstick and tile patterns, the 10th and 20th term, and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Find the rule by checking every step. To reach the 10th term, add 9 jumps to the 1st term.
key_sub: 0.5, 1, 2, 4 is Multiply by 2, not Add 0.5. Start at 0.5 and add 0.25: the 10th term is 0.5 + 9 × 0.25 = 2.75.
body_html:
A rule makes the pattern

Each number in a pattern is a term. Its place in the pattern is the term number (1st, 2nd, 3rd …). A rule tells you how to get the next term, such as Add 0.25, Subtract 14 or Multiply by 2.

Decimals

0.35, 0.65, 0.95, 1.25, ?

The difference is 0.3 each time. Line up the decimal points: 1.25 + 0.30 = 1.55.

Answer: 1.55

Fractions

13, 23, 1, 1 13, ?

The rule is Add 13. 1 13 + 13 = 1 23.

Answer: 1 23

Check every step to find the rule

Work out the difference between each pair of terms. If it is always the same, the rule adds or subtracts it. If the jumps keep growing, try multiplying.

Find the rule

0.5, 1, 2, 4, …

The jumps are 0.5, 1, 2, so it is not Add 0.5. Each term is 2 times the one before.

Answer: Multiply by 2

Growing patterns

Count the pieces in each figure, then find how many are added each time. Put the counts in a table.

Jump to the 10th or 20th term

From the 1st term to the 10th term there are 9 jumps. Add the start and the jumps.

10th term

Start at 0.5. The rule is Add 0.25. What is the 10th term?

9 jumps: 9 × 0.25 = 2.25. 0.5 + 2.25 = 2.75.

Answer: 2.75

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
1.25 + 0.3 = 1.28Line up the decimal points: 1.25 + 0.30 = 1.55
Using only the first step: 0.5, 1, 2, 4 is Add 0.5Check every step. Growing jumps mean multiply
10th term = start + 10 jumpsFrom the 1st to the 10th term there are 9 jumps
4 matchsticks for Figure 1, so 4 × 10 = 40 for Figure 10Each figure adds 3, not 4: 4 + 9 × 3 = 31
“Which term is 10?” answered with the 10th termThe term number and the term are different. Find how many jumps make 10

faq.q: What are number patterns in Year 6 maths?
faq.a: In the Australian Curriculum (AC9M6A01), Year 6 students use rules to continue patterns with whole numbers, decimals and fractions, such as 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, and growing patterns made from matchsticks or tiles. They also find the rule and use it to work out terms further along.

faq.q: How do you find the rule for a number pattern?
faq.a: Work out the difference between each pair of terms. If it is always the same, the rule adds or subtracts it (for example Add 0.4); if the jumps keep growing, check whether each term is multiplied by the same number, such as Multiply by 2.

faq.q: How do you find the 20th term of a pattern?
faq.a: Count the jumps from the 1st term: there are 19. Multiply the rule by 19 and add it to the 1st term, so for 2.4, 2.8, 3.2, … the 20th term is 2.4 + 19 × 0.4 = 10.
No. NAPLAN is sat in Years 3, 5, 7 and 9. Patterns and rules are part of the Year 7 NAPLAN numeracy test, so Year 6 is a good time to practise them.

sets.title: Continue the pattern: decimals and fractions

items.q:
What is the next term?
0.6, 1, 1.4, 1.8, ?
items.e: The rule is Add 0.4: 0.6 + 0.4 = 1. So the next term is 1.8 + 0.4 = 2.2. Line up the decimal points: 1.8 + 0.4 is not 1.12.

items.q:
What is the next term?
0.9, 1.7, 2.5, 3.3, ?
items.e: The rule is Add 0.8: 0.9 + 0.8 = 1.7. So the next term is 3.3 + 0.8 = 4.1. Line up the decimal points: 3.3 + 0.8 is not 3.11.

items.q:
What is the next term?
0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, ?
items.e: The rule is Add 0.25: 0.25 + 0.25 = 0.5. So the next term is 1 + 0.25 = 1.25.

items.q:
What is the next term?
1.5, 2.75, 4, 5.25, ?
items.e: The rule is Add 1.25: 1.5 + 1.25 = 2.75. So the next term is 5.25 + 1.25 = 6.5.

items.q:
What is the next term?
1.75, 2.5, 3.25, 4, ?
items.e: The rule is Add 0.75: 1.75 + 0.75 = 2.5. So the next term is 4 + 0.75 = 4.75.

items.q:
What is the next term?
0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, ?
items.e: The rule is Add 0.5: 0.5 + 0.5 = 1. So the next term is 2 + 0.5 = 2.5.

items.q:
What is the next term?
0.35, 0.65, 0.95, 1.25, ?
items.e: The rule is Add 0.3: 0.35 + 0.3 = 0.65. So the next term is 1.25 + 0.3 = 1.55. Line up the decimal points: 1.25 + 0.3 is not 1.28.

items.q:
What is the next term?
0.05, 0.2, 0.35, 0.5, ?
items.e: The rule is Add 0.15: 0.05 + 0.15 = 0.2. So the next term is 0.5 + 0.15 = 0.65. Line up the decimal points: 0.5 + 0.15 is not 0.2.

items.q:
What is the next term?
6.2, 5.5, 4.8, 4.1, ?
items.e: The terms get smaller, so the rule subtracts: 6.2 − 0.7 = 5.5. Next: 4.1 − 0.7 = 3.4.

items.q:
What is the next term?
10, 9.25, 8.5, 7.75, ?
items.e: The terms get smaller, so the rule subtracts: 10 − 0.75 = 9.25. Next: 7.75 − 0.75 = 7.

items.q:
What is the next term?
3, 2.6, 2.2, 1.8, ?
items.e: The terms get smaller, so the rule subtracts: 3 − 0.4 = 2.6. Next: 1.8 − 0.4 = 1.4.

items.q:
What is the next term?
23, 1 13, 2, 2 23, ?
items.e: The rule is Add 23: 23 + 23 = 1 13. Next: 2 23 + 23 = 3 13.

items.q:
What is the next term?
5, 4 34, 4 12, 4 14, ?
items.e: The rule is Subtract 14: 5 − 14 = 4 34. Next: 4 14 − 14 = 4.

items.q:
What is the next term?
12, 2, 3 12, 5, ?
items.e: The rule is Add 1 12: 12 + 1 12 = 2. Next: 5 + 1 12 = 6 12.

items.q:
What is the next term?
13, 23, 1, 1 13, ?
items.e: The rule is Add 13: 13 + 13 = 23. Next: 1 13 + 13 = 1 23.

items.q:
What is the next term?
14, 12, 34, 1, ?
items.e: The rule is Add 14: 14 + 14 = 12. Next: 1 + 14 = 1 14.

items.q:
What is the next term?
0.1, 0.3, 0.9, 2.7, ?
items.e: The jumps are 0.2, 0.6, 1.8, so the rule is not adding the same amount. Each term is 3 times the one before: 0.1 × 3 = 0.3, 0.3 × 3 = 0.9, 0.9 × 3 = 2.7. Next: 2.7 × 3 = 8.1.

items.q:
What is the next term?
0.5, 1, 2, 4, ?
items.e: The jumps are 0.5, 1, 2, so the rule is not adding the same amount. Each term is 2 times the one before: 0.5 × 2 = 1, 1 × 2 = 2, 2 × 2 = 4. Next: 4 × 2 = 8.

items.q:
What is the next term?
0.2, 0.4, 0.8, 1.6, ?
items.e: The jumps are 0.2, 0.4, 0.8, so the rule is not adding the same amount. Each term is 2 times the one before: 0.2 × 2 = 0.4, 0.4 × 2 = 0.8, 0.8 × 2 = 1.6. Next: 1.6 × 2 = 3.2.

items.q:
What is the next term?
1.5, 3, 6, 12, ?
items.e: The jumps are 1.5, 3, 6, so the rule is not adding the same amount. Each term is 2 times the one before: 1.5 × 2 = 3, 3 × 2 = 6, 6 × 2 = 12. Next: 12 × 2 = 24.

sets.title: Find the rule and the missing term

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
5, 4.4, 3.8, 3.2, …
items.e: Find the difference between each pair of terms: 5 − 4.4 = 0.6, 4.4 − 3.8 = 0.6, 3.8 − 3.2 = 0.6. The difference is always 0.6, so the rule is Subtract 0.6.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
0.08, 0.12, 0.16, 0.2, …
items.e: Find the difference between each pair of terms: 0.12 − 0.08 = 0.04, 0.16 − 0.12 = 0.04, 0.2 − 0.16 = 0.04. The difference is always 0.04, so the rule is Add 0.04.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
0.3, 0.55, 0.8, 1.05, …
items.e: Find the difference between each pair of terms: 0.55 − 0.3 = 0.25, 0.8 − 0.55 = 0.25, 1.05 − 0.8 = 0.25. The difference is always 0.25, so the rule is Add 0.25.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
3.6, 4.8, 6, 7.2, …
items.e: Find the difference between each pair of terms: 4.8 − 3.6 = 1.2, 6 − 4.8 = 1.2, 7.2 − 6 = 1.2. The difference is always 1.2, so the rule is Add 1.2.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
2.5, 3.25, 4, 4.75, …
items.e: Find the difference between each pair of terms: 3.25 − 2.5 = 0.75, 4 − 3.25 = 0.75, 4.75 − 4 = 0.75. The difference is always 0.75, so the rule is Add 0.75.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
1.2, 1.6, 2, 2.4, …
items.e: Find the difference between each pair of terms: 1.6 − 1.2 = 0.4, 2 − 1.6 = 0.4, 2.4 − 2 = 0.4. The difference is always 0.4, so the rule is Add 0.4.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
12, 34, 1, 1 14, …
items.e: Each term is 14 more than the one before: 12 + 14 = 34, 34 + 14 = 1, 1 + 14 = 1 14. The rule is Add 14.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
4, 3 14, 2 12, 1 34, …
items.e: Each term is 34 less than the one before: 4 − 34 = 3 14, 3 14 − 34 = 2 12, 2 12 − 34 = 1 34. The rule is Subtract 34.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
23, 1 13, 2, 2 23, …
items.e: Each term is 23 more than the one before: 23 + 23 = 1 13, 1 13 + 23 = 2, 2 + 23 = 2 23. The rule is Add 23. Multiply by 2 works only for the first step (23 × 2 = 1 13); 1 13 × 2 is not 2.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
3, 2 34, 2 12, 2 14, …
items.e: Each term is 14 less than the one before: 3 − 14 = 2 34, 2 34 − 14 = 2 12, 2 12 − 14 = 2 14. The rule is Subtract 14.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
15, 35, 1, 1 25, …
items.e: Each term is 25 more than the one before: 15 + 25 = 35, 35 + 25 = 1, 1 + 25 = 1 25. The rule is Add 25.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
13, 23, 1, 1 13, …
items.e: Each term is 13 more than the one before: 13 + 13 = 23, 23 + 13 = 1, 1 + 13 = 1 13. The rule is Add 13. Multiply by 2 works only for the first step (13 × 2 = 23); 23 × 2 is not 1.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
0.5, 1, 2, 4, …
items.e: The differences are 0.5, 1, 2, so the rule is not adding or subtracting the same amount. 0.5 × 2 = 1, 1 × 2 = 2, 2 × 2 = 4. The rule is Multiply by 2.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
80, 40, 20, 10, …
items.e: The differences are 40, 20, 10, so the rule is not adding or subtracting the same amount. 80 ÷ 2 = 40, 40 ÷ 2 = 20, 20 ÷ 2 = 10. The rule is Divide by 2.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
6, 3, 1 12, 34, …
items.e: The differences are 3, 1 12, 34, so the rule is not adding or subtracting the same amount. 6 ÷ 2 = 3, 3 ÷ 2 = 1 12, 1 12 ÷ 2 = 34. The rule is Divide by 2.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
0.03, 0.3, 3, 30, …
items.e: The differences are 0.27, 2.7, 27, so the rule is not adding or subtracting the same amount. 0.03 × 10 = 0.3, 0.3 × 10 = 3, 3 × 10 = 30. The rule is Multiply by 10.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
0.2, 0.6, 1.8, 5.4, …
items.e: The differences are 0.4, 1.2, 3.6, so the rule is not adding or subtracting the same amount. 0.2 × 3 = 0.6, 0.6 × 3 = 1.8, 1.8 × 3 = 5.4. The rule is Multiply by 3.

items.q:
What is the missing term?
0.4, 1.2, ?, 10.8, 32.4
items.e: The jumps grow, so look for multiplying: 0.4 × 3 = 1.2. The missing term is 1.2 × 3 = 3.6. Check: 3.6 × 3 = 10.8.

items.q:
What is the missing term?
14, 34, ?, 1 34, 2 14
items.e: The rule is Add 12 (14 + 12 = 34). The missing term is 34 + 12 = 1 14. Check: 1 14 + 12 = 1 34. Do not add the tops and the bottoms: 34 + 12 is not 46.

items.q:
What is the missing term?
2.5, 3.25, ?, 4.75, 5.5
items.e: The rule is Add 0.75 (2.5 + 0.75 = 3.25). The missing term is 3.25 + 0.75 = 4. Check: 4 + 0.75 = 4.75.

items.q: How many matchsticks will Figure 4 need?
items.e: Count each figure: 4, 7, 10. Each figure adds 3 matchsticks. Figure 4: 10 + 3 = 13.

items.q: How many matchsticks will Figure 4 need?
items.e: Count each figure: 3, 5, 7. Each figure adds 2 matchsticks. Figure 4: 7 + 2 = 9.

items.q: How many tiles will Figure 4 need?
items.e: Count each figure: 5, 9, 13. Each figure adds 4 tiles. Figure 4: 13 + 4 = 17.

items.q: How many matchsticks will Figure 4 need?
items.e: Count each figure: 6, 11, 16. Each figure adds 5 matchsticks. Figure 4: 16 + 5 = 21.

items.q: How many tiles will Figure 4 need?
items.e: Count each figure: 3, 5, 7. Each figure adds 2 tiles. Figure 4: 7 + 2 = 9.

items.q: Which rule gives the number of matchsticks for any figure?
items.e: Each figure adds 3, so multiply the figure number by 3. Figure 1: 3 × 1 = 3, and it has 4, so add 1. Check Figure 3: 3 × 3 + 1 = 10. (4 × figure number works only for Figure 1.)

items.q: Which rule gives the number of tiles for any figure?
items.e: Each figure adds 4, so multiply the figure number by 4. Figure 1: 4 × 1 = 4, and it has 5, so add 1. Check Figure 3: 4 × 3 + 1 = 13. (5 × figure number works only for Figure 1.)

items.q: Which rule describes how the pattern grows?
items.e: Count the tiles: 4, 6, 8. Figure 1 has 4, and each new figure adds 2 (6 − 4 = 2). Adding 4 each time would give 8, not 6, for Figure 2.

items.q: Which rule describes how the pattern grows?
items.e: Count the matchsticks: 6, 11, 16. Figure 1 has 6, and each new figure adds 5 (11 − 6 = 5). Adding 6 each time would give 12, not 11, for Figure 2.

items.q: The pattern keeps growing in the same way. What number goes in the box under Figure 10?
items.e: Each figure adds 5. From Figure 1 to Figure 10 there are 9 jumps: 6 + 9 × 5 = 51. (Adding 5 to the last number gives Figure 5, not Figure 10.)

items.q: The pattern keeps growing in the same way. What number goes in the box under Figure 20?
items.e: Each figure adds 2. From Figure 1 to Figure 20 there are 19 jumps: 4 + 19 × 2 = 42. (Adding 2 to the last number gives Figure 5, not Figure 20.)

items.q: The pattern keeps growing in the same way. What number goes in the box under Figure 10?
items.e: Each figure adds 3. From Figure 1 to Figure 10 there are 9 jumps: 5 + 9 × 3 = 32. (Adding 3 to the last number gives Figure 5, not Figure 10.)

items.q: The pattern keeps growing in the same way. What number goes in the box under Figure 20?
items.e: Each figure adds 2. From Figure 1 to Figure 20 there are 19 jumps: 3 + 19 × 2 = 41. (Adding 2 to the last number gives Figure 5, not Figure 20.)

items.q: How many tiles will Figure 20 need?
items.e: Figure 1 has 3 and each figure adds 2. From Figure 1 to Figure 20 there are 19 jumps: 3 + 19 × 2 = 41.

items.q: How many matchsticks will Figure 10 need?
items.e: Figure 1 has 3 and each figure adds 2. From Figure 1 to Figure 10 there are 9 jumps: 3 + 9 × 2 = 21.

items.q: How many matchsticks will Figure 10 need?
items.e: Figure 1 has 6 and each figure adds 5. From Figure 1 to Figure 10 there are 9 jumps: 6 + 9 × 5 = 51.

items.q: How many tiles will Figure 10 need?
items.e: Figure 1 has 5 and each figure adds 4. From Figure 1 to Figure 10 there are 9 jumps: 5 + 9 × 4 = 41.

items.q: Which figure will use exactly 31 matchsticks?
items.e: After Figure 1 there are 31 − 4 = 27 more matchsticks, which is 27 ÷ 3 = 9 jumps. 1 + 9 = 10, so it is Figure 10. Check: 4 + 9 × 3 = 31.

items.q: Which figure will use exactly 25 tiles?
items.e: After Figure 1 there are 25 − 3 = 22 more tiles, which is 22 ÷ 2 = 11 jumps. 1 + 11 = 12, so it is Figure 12. Check: 3 + 11 × 2 = 25.

items.q: Which figure will use exactly 41 matchsticks?
items.e: After Figure 1 there are 41 − 6 = 35 more matchsticks, which is 35 ÷ 5 = 7 jumps. 1 + 7 = 8, so it is Figure 8. Check: 6 + 7 × 5 = 41.

items.q: Start at 0.5. The rule is Add 0.25. What is the 10th term?
items.e: From the 1st term to the 10th term there are 9 jumps, not 10. 9 × 0.25 = 2.25, and 0.5 + 2.25 = 2.75.

items.q: Start at 2. The rule is Add 34. What is the 10th term?
items.e: From the 1st term to the 10th term there are 9 jumps, not 10. 9 × 34 = 6 34, and 2 + 6 34 = 8 34.

items.q: Start at 13. The rule is Add 13. What is the 20th term?
items.e: From the 1st term to the 20th term there are 19 jumps, not 20. 19 × 13 = 6 13, and 13 + 6 13 = 6 23.

items.q: Start at 3. The rule is Add 1.5. What is the 20th term?
items.e: From the 1st term to the 20th term there are 19 jumps, not 20. 19 × 1.5 = 28.5, and 3 + 28.5 = 31.5.

items.q: Start at 20. The rule is Subtract 0.75. What is the 10th term?
items.e: From the 1st term to the 10th term there are 9 jumps, not 10. 9 × 0.75 = 6.75, and 20 − 6.75 = 13.25.

items.q: Start at 1.2. The rule is Add 0.4. What is the 10th term?
items.e: From the 1st term to the 10th term there are 9 jumps, not 10. 9 × 0.4 = 3.6, and 1.2 + 3.6 = 4.8.

items.q:
1 12, 2, 2 12, 3, …
What is the 10th term?
items.e: The rule is Add 12. The 10th term is 9 jumps after the 1st term: 1 12 + 9 × 12 = 1 12 + 4 12 = 6. 10 is the term number, not the term.

items.q:
14, 12, 34, 1, …
What is the 20th term?
items.e: The rule is Add 14. The 20th term is 19 jumps after the 1st term: 14 + 19 × 14 = 14 + 4 34 = 5. 20 is the term number, not the term.

items.q:
9.6, 9.2, 8.8, 8.4, …
What is the 10th term?
items.e: The rule is Subtract 0.4. The 10th term is 9 jumps after the 1st term: 9.6 − 9 × 0.4 = 9.6 − 3.6 = 6. 10 is the term number, not the term.

items.q:
2.4, 2.8, 3.2, 3.6, …
What is the 20th term?
items.e: The rule is Add 0.4. The 20th term is 19 jumps after the 1st term: 2.4 + 19 × 0.4 = 2.4 + 7.6 = 10. 20 is the term number, not the term.

items.q: The pattern continues. What is the term in position 20?
items.e: Each term is the position × 0.4 (1 × 0.4 = 0.4, 4 × 0.4 = 1.6). So position 20: 20 × 0.4 = 8.

items.q: The pattern continues. What is the term in position 10?
items.e: The terms go up by 2, so multiply the position by 2, then add 0.5 (1 × 2 + 0.5 = 2.5). Position 10: 10 × 2 + 0.5 = 20.5.

items.q:
The rule for the term is position × 1.5 + 2.
What is the 20th term?
items.e: Multiply first, then add: 20 × 1.5 = 30, and 30 + 2 = 32.

items.q: The pattern continues. What is the term in position 10?
items.e: Each term is the position × 0.75 (1 × 0.75 = 0.75, 4 × 0.75 = 3). So position 10: 10 × 0.75 = 7.5.

items.q: The pattern continues. What is the term in position 20?
items.e: Each term is the position × 0.3 (1 × 0.3 = 0.3, 4 × 0.3 = 1.2). So position 20: 20 × 0.3 = 6.

items.q:
14, 34, 1 14, 1 34, …
Which term is 4 34?
items.e: 4 34 − 14 = 4 12, and 4 12 ÷ 12 = 9 jumps. The 1st term plus 9 jumps is the 10th term. Check: 14 + 9 × 12 = 4 34.
10 − 3 = 7, and 7 ÷ 0.5 = 14 jumps. The 1st term plus 14 jumps is the 15th term. Check: 3 + 14 × 0.5 = 10.
9 − 1.5 = 7.5, and 7.5 ÷ 0.75 = 10 jumps. The 1st term plus 10 jumps is the 11th term. Check: 1.5 + 10 × 0.75 = 9.

items.q: Start at 0.1. The rule is Multiply by 10. What is the 6th term?
items.e: 0.1, 1, 10, 100, 1000, 10 000. From the 1st to the 6th term there are 5 jumps, so multiply by 10 five times.

items.q:
1, 2, 4, 8, …
What is the 10th term?
items.e: The rule is Multiply by 2. Keep doubling: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512. The 10th term is 512.

items.q: Matilda has $150 in the bank and spends $12.50 each week. After how many weeks will she have $50 left?
items.e: Matilda spends $150 − $50 = $100. $100 ÷ $12.50 = 8 weeks. ($150 ÷ $12.50 = 12 weeks would leave $0.)

items.q: Amelia builds a fence. 1 section uses 2 posts and 3 rails (5 pieces). Each extra section adds 1 post and 3 rails. How many pieces are needed for 12 sections?
items.e: Each extra section adds 4 pieces, because it shares a post. 5 + 11 × 4 = 49. (12 × 5 = 60 counts shared posts twice.)

items.q: A taxi trip costs $4.20 to start plus $1.60 for each kilometre. How much is a 10 km trip?
items.e: 10 × $1.60 = $16. Add the start cost once: $16 + $4.20 = $20.20. ($58 adds $4.20 to every kilometre.)

items.q: At an outdoor concert, row 1 has 18 seats. Each row has 2 more seats than the row in front. How many seats are in row 20?
items.e: Row 1 to row 20 is 19 jumps: 19 × 2 = 38. 18 + 38 = 56 seats.

items.q: A rainwater tank holds 250 L. The garden uses 12.5 L a day and no rain falls. How much water is left after 8 days?
items.e: 8 × 12.5 = 100 L used. 250 − 100 = 150 L left. (100 L is the amount used, not the amount left.)

items.q: A jug holds 3 L of cordial. Each glass uses 14 L. How much is left after 7 glasses?
items.e: 7 glasses use 7 × 14 = 74 = 1 34 L. 3 − 1 34 = 1 14 L.

items.q: One lap of the school oval is 0.4 km. How many laps does Grace need to run 6 km?
items.e: Count by 0.4: 2 km is 5 laps, so 6 km is 3 × 5 = 15 laps. Check: 15 × 0.4 = 6.

items.q: Square tables are pushed together in a row for a class party. 1 table seats 4 students, and each extra table adds 2 seats. How many students can sit at 15 tables?
items.e: The pattern is 4, 6, 8, … (add 2). 15 tables: 4 + 14 × 2 = 32. It is not 15 × 4 = 60, because seats are lost where tables touch.

items.q: A candle is 24 cm tall. It burns down 1.5 cm each hour. How tall is it after 8 hours?
items.e: 8 × 1.5 = 12 cm burns away. 24 − 12 = 12 cm left.

items.q: In week 1, Isla walks 2 km to school and back each day. Each week she adds 34 km. How far does she walk each day in week 5?
items.e: Week 1 to week 5 is 4 jumps: 4 × 34 = 3 km. 2 + 3 = 5 km.

items.q: Ethan starts with nothing and saves $2.50 a week. After how many weeks will he have $40?
items.e: Count by $2.50: $10 is 4 weeks, so $40 is 4 × 4 = 16 weeks. Check: 16 × $2.50 = $40.

items.q: Jack has $12 in his money box. He saves $2.50 a week. How much money will he have after 8 weeks?
Sienna runs 1.5 km on day 1 of her training. Each day she runs 0.25 km more. How far does she run on day 10?
items.e: From day 1 to day 10 there are 9 jumps: 9 × 0.25 = 2.25 km. 1.5 + 2.25 = 3.75 km.

items.q: A seedling is 4.5 cm tall. It grows 1.2 cm each week. How tall is it after 6 weeks?
items.e: 6 weeks of growth: 6 × 1.2 = 7.2 cm. 4.5 + 7.2 = 11.7 cm.

items.q: A 64 cm ribbon is cut in half. One half is cut in half again, and so on. How long is the piece after 5 cuts?
items.e: Each cut halves the length: 32, 16, 8, 4, 2 cm. (54 cm subtracts 2 each time instead of halving.)

items.q: Netball finals tickets cost $7.50 each. 1 ticket costs $7.50, 2 tickets cost $15. How much do 12 tickets cost?
items.e: Each ticket adds $7.50, so multiply: 12 × $7.50 = $90.00. ($19.50 adds 12 instead of multiplying.)

items.q: Zara gets $5 pocket money a week at age 6. It goes up by $0.50 each birthday. How much does she get a week at age 12?
items.e: Age 6 to age 12 is 6 birthdays: 6 × $0.50 = $3. $5 + $3 = $8.00. ($11 adds $1 a year instead of $0.50.)

items.q: At 6 pm it is 24°C. The temperature falls 1.5°C each hour. What is the temperature at 11 pm?
A sheet of paper is folded in half again and again. After 1 fold there are 2 layers, after 2 folds there are 4 layers. How many layers are there after 6 folds?
items.e: Each fold doubles the layers: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64. Adding 2 each time (12) uses the wrong kind of rule.

items.q: For footy pre-season, Harper runs 2.5 km in week 1 and 0.5 km more each week. In which week will she run 6 km?
items.e: 6 − 2.5 = 3.5 km more. 3.5 ÷ 0.5 = 7 jumps. Week 1 + 7 jumps is week 8. Check: 2.5 + 7 × 0.5 = 6.
